title: Outposts and weak squares
summary: An outpost is a square deep in enemy land that no enemy pawn can attack. A knight there is very strong.
body:
### A square no pawn can attack

An **outpost** is a square in the enemy half of the board. One of your pawns guards it, and no enemy pawn can attack it. A knight on an outpost is very strong. Your opponent cannot chase it away with a pawn. It hits many squares near the enemy king.

How to find an outpost:

- A pawn attacks only the two squares diagonally in front of it. A pawn cannot go back.
- So look for a square that no enemy pawn guards now, and none can guard later. This is a **hole**, or weak square.
- Check that one of your own pawns can guard that square.

Two examples:

- Black has no c-pawn and no e-pawn. No pawn can attack d5 soon. Your pawn on e4 guards it.
- Black plays ...d5 and ...f5. These pawns cannot go back to d6 or f6. So no pawn can attack e5 soon. A white knight on e5, guarded by the d4 pawn, is very strong. London players know this square well.

How to use an outpost:

- Put a knight there. A bishop can also be good there.
- Pawns cannot chase your piece, but enemy pieces can still take it. Trade or avoid those pieces.
- Check the route. Do not stop on a square that a pawn can attack. A knight on b5 can be hit by ...a6.

How to avoid giving one away:

- Think before every pawn move. Pawns never come back. The squares they stop guarding stay weak.

Rule of thumb: put a knight on a square that no enemy pawn can attack, and think before you push a pawn.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Black has no c-pawn and no e-pawn. Put your knight on an outpost.
exercises.explanation: Nd5 stands on a hole. Black has no c-pawn and no e-pawn, so no pawn can attack d5 soon. The e4 pawn guards it. Nb5 is worse: Black plays ...a6.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Black has pawns on d5 and f5. Put a knight on the outpost in the centre.
exercises.explanation: Black's pawns on d5 and f5 have passed d6 and f6. So no black pawn can attack e5 soon. The d4 pawn guards the knight. Ne4 is no outpost: the pawns on d5 and f5 attack it.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. White has no c-pawn and no e-pawn. Put your knight on an outpost.
exercises.explanation: Nd4 is guarded by the e5 pawn. White has no c-pawn and no e-pawn, so no pawn can attack d4 soon. Nb4 is worse: White plays a3.
